title: Burp Suite
text:
1. Overview
Burp is a GUI tool for inspecting and editing web traffic. Use Proxy for requests, Repeater for manual experiments, and licensed Pro features where available. This is an educational section, not an automation target.

2. Setup
License: Not detected. Community/Pro detection is unknown. Use Burp's built-in browser, or follow the vendor's external-browser proxy and CA-certificate instructions. SecDesk never changes system proxies or installs a CA.

3. Workflow cheatsheet
Proxy: inspect authorized traffic. Intercept: pause an individual request. Repeater: edit and resend it manually. Intruder/Scanner capabilities depend on the installed edition and license. Set the target scope in Burp before testing.

4. Successful example
Unverified: no native run or output has been captured. Follow the vendor's getting-started labs; no result is invented here.

5. Failed example
Unverified: no native failure output has been captured.

6. Error dictionary
Native patterns remain unverified. Consult vendor proxy-listener, browser-configuration and certificate troubleshooting. Do not disable TLS verification as a workaround.

7. Launch
Use the installed vendor application. Native shortcut and optional Pro REST integration require installation/license verification; they are not enabled here. This section does not run scans.
Source: https://portswigger.net/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/proxy
External browser: https://portswigger.net/burp/documentation/desktop/external-browser-config

title: Device companion
text:
1. Overview
PC-side USB-serial companion for your DIY device. No firmware capabilities are assumed.

2. Setup
Firmware command protocol, USB vendor/product IDs, baud rate and framing are required. They have not been supplied. Local port discovery does not open a connection or identify any port as your device.

3. Requested features
Sub-GHz capture/replay; 125 kHz RFID read; NFC read/emulate; infrared capture/replay; BadUSB upload; GPIO. All device actions remain disabled until the real protocol and capability set are supplied.

4. Successful example
Unverified: no matching device, adapter or capture output is available.

5. Failed example
Firmware protocol and USB IDs required; device actions disabled. This is SecDesk's local guard, not fabricated device output.

6. Error dictionary
Adapter missing: supply the firmware specification. Device mismatch: select a port matching the supplied VID/PID. Incomplete write: outcome is unknown; no command is repeated. Native firmware error patterns are unknown.

7. Connection
Check USB ports reads local metadata only. The pluggable FirmwareAdapter and CompanionTransport require explicit authorization for every supported operation. No transmit, replay, emulation, BadUSB or GPIO command is guessed or sent.
Source: https://pyserial.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools.html#serial-tools-list-ports
